label: <DEL> step when sequence starts with two tokens from {3,r,o,p,z,x,f,t,s}
explanation: 89% of activation mass is at the delimiter step (t == L), where the unit is active on about 11% of sequences. It never fires in the copy phase and never at t <= 3. Which sequences it fires on depends mostly on the first original tokens: lift is highest for first_tok in {3,r,o,p,z} and then {x,f,t,s}, with the same ordering for orig(1), and rate goes up with L (9.8% of DEL steps at L=9). The remaining 11% of mass is weak activity on late original-phase steps (t >= 4) of long sequences that start with the same tokens, ramping toward the DEL step. The predicate (DEL step and orig(0), orig(1) both in the set) gets dev P 0.65, R 0.46, F1 0.54. Phase==1 alone covers 89% of mass at 0.11 precision. It looks like a graded readout of a stored first-token code, not a clean binary feature.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: 3, o, r, z, p, x; least: a, b, u, 0) and the second original token (most: 3, r, o, s, z, x; least: y, b, h, k); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=7, t=8.
